body: {"items":[{"id":"2026-20411","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20411/airworthiness-directives-airbus-helicopters","summary":"The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-12-09, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Model AS350B, AS350BA, AS350B1, and AS350D helicopters. AD 2026-12-09 requires revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing maintenance manual (MM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-12-09, a determination was made that new and more restrictive airworthiness limitations and maintenance tasks are necessary. This proposed AD would require incorporating these airworthiness limitations into the ALS of the existing MM or ICA and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20393","title":"Airworthiness Directives; DG Aviation GmbH (Type Certificate Previously Held by DG Flugzeugbau GmbH) Gliders","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20393/airworthiness-directives-dg-aviation-gmbh-type-certificate-previously-held-by-dg-flugzeugbau-gmbh","summary":"The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-13-08, which applies to all DG Aviation GmbH Model DG-1000T gliders. AD 2025-13-08 requires revising the glider flight manual and installing \"Motor INOP\" placards to prohibit operation with the powerplant. Since issuance of AD 2025-13-08, a design improvement to the propeller adapter ring has been developed that is considered terminating action for the operational prohibition of AD 2025-13-08. This proposed AD would retain the requirement to revise the flight manual, would provide an optional terminating action for the retained actions by incorporating a specified modification, would allow removal of the \"Motor INOP\" placards following accomplishment of that optional terminating action, and would require removal, inspection, and reinstallation of the propeller adapter disk, including installation of safety pins. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected propeller adapter rings. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20392","title":"Overpressure Blast Effects Analysis Burden Reducing Clarification","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20392/overpressure-blast-effects-analysis-burden-reducing-clarification","summary":"FAA proposes to amend its commercial space launch and reentry licensing regulations to streamline the licensing process and reduce regulatory burden for license applicants. Specifically, FAA proposes to amend the regulations to state that a far-field overpressure blast effects analysis required for license applicants does not need to account for members of the public in hypothetical locations.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20391","title":"Lightning Hazard Mitigation Burden-Reducing Exception","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20391/lightning-hazard-mitigation-burden-reducing-exception","summary":"FAA proposes to amend its commercial space launch and reentry licensing regulations to streamline the licensing process and reduce regulatory burden for license applicants. Specifically, FAA proposes to add an exception for compliance with lightning hazard mitigation requirements for certain licensed launch and reentry operations.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20388","title":"Streamlining Flight Safety Analysis Methodology Means of Compliance","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20388/streamlining-flight-safety-analysis-methodology-means-of-compliance","summary":"FAA proposes to amend its commercial space launch and reentry licensing regulations to streamline the licensing process. Specifically, FAA proposes to alleviate regulatory burden for license applicants by consolidating information required for an operator's flight safety analysis.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20387","title":"Digital Modernization for Licensing Electronic Application Submissions","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20387/digital-modernization-for-licensing-electronic-application-submissions","summary":"FAA proposes to amend its commercial space launch and reentry licensing regulations to allow for submission of license and permit applications and requests for waivers, alternative time frames, and safety element approvals through additional electronic methods.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20386","title":"Simplifying Physical Containment Requirements","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20386/simplifying-physical-containment-requirements","summary":"FAA proposes to amend its commercial space launch and reentry licensing regulations to streamline the licensing process and reduce regulatory burden on operators. Specifically, FAA proposes to relieve the burden by specifying that, when using physical containment as a hazard control strategy, operators do not need to develop flight hazard areas in accordance with FAA's existing flight hazard area analysis requirements.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20372","title":"Amendment of Domestic Very High Frequency Omnidirectional Range (VOR) Federal Airways V-16, V-184, and Revocation of V-284 and V-577; Eastern United States","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20372/amendment-of-domestic-very-high-frequency-omnidirectional-range-vor-federal-airways-v-16-v-184-and","summary":"This action proposes to amend domestic Very High Frequency Omnidirectional Range (VOR) Federal Airways V-16, V-184, and revoke V- 284 and V-577 in the eastern United States. The FAA is proposing these actions due to the planned decommissioning of the Cedar Lake, NJ (VCN), VOR/Distance Measuring Equipment (DME).","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20358","title":"Notice of Buy America Waiver for North County Transit District DMU Replacement Parts","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20358/notice-of-buy-america-waiver-for-north-county-transit-district-dmu-replacement-parts","summary":"The Federal Transit Administration (\"FTA\") is granting a waiver of Buy America domestic preferences for North County Transit District (\"NCTD\") to procure certain replacement parts for twelve Siemens Desiro series diesel multiple unit (\"DMU\") vehicles.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20355","title":"Extension of a Previously Approved Collection: Public Charters, 14 CFR Part 380","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20355/extension-of-a-previously-approved-collection-public-charters-14-cfr-part-380","summary":"In compliance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, Public Law 104-13, the Department of Transportation (DOT) invites the general public, industry and other governmental parties to comment on Public Charters, 14 CFR part 380. The pre-existing information collection request was previously approved by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB).","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20350","title":"Special Conditions: Honda Aircraft Company LLC Model HA-480 Airplane; High Altitude Operation","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20350/special-conditions-honda-aircraft-company-llc-model-ha-480-airplane-high-altitude-operation","summary":"This action proposes special conditions for the Honda Aircraft Company LLC (Honda) Model HA-480 airplane. This airplane will have a novel or unusual design feature when compared to the state of technology envisioned in the airworthiness standards for normal category airplanes. This airplane will have design features associated with high altitude operations up to 47,000 feet. The applicable airworthiness regulations do not contain adequate or appropriate safety standards for this design feature. These proposed special conditions contain the additional safety standards that the Administrator considers necessary to establish a level of safety equivalent to that established by the existing airworthiness standards.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20327","title":"AC 187-1V: Schedule of Charges Outside the United States","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20327/ac-187-1v-schedule-of-charges-outside-the-united-states","summary":"The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is announcing the availability of Advisory Circular (AC) 187-1V which transmits an updated schedule of charges for services of FAA Flight Standards Aviation Safety Inspectors outside the United States. The advisory circular has been updated in accordance with the procedures listed in 14 CFR part 187, Appendix A.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20325","title":"Clarification to the Applicability of Emergency Exemptions; Response to Petitions for Reconsideration","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20325/clarification-to-the-applicability-of-emergency-exemptions-response-to-petitions-for-reconsideration","summary":"FMCSA amends its emergency declaration regulations to revise from 14 days to 30 days the length of the relief automatically triggered subsequent to a regional declaration of emergency by a Governor of a State, the Governor's authorized representative, or FMCSA. This action is in response to several petitions for reconsideration received after publication of a final rule in October 2023.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20323","title":"Notice of Request To Release Airport Property","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20323/notice-of-request-to-release-airport-property","summary":"The FAA proposes to rule and invites public comment on the release and sale of two parcels of land at the Liberal Mid-America Regional Airport (LBL), Liberal, Kansas, under the provisions of 49 U.S.C. 47107(h)(2).","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20312","title":"Notice of Intent To Designate as Abandoned VanDyke Russell Supplemental Type Certificate","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20312/notice-of-intent-to-designate-as-abandoned-vandyke-russell-supplemental-type-certificate","summary":"This notice announces the FAA's intent to designate VanDyke Russell Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) No. SA176CE as abandoned and make the related engineering data available upon request. The FAA has been unsuccessful in contacting VanDyke Russell concerning the STC. This action is intended to enhance aviation safety.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20306","title":"Notice To Reestablish the Transit Advisory Committee for Safety Charter","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20306/notice-to-reestablish-the-transit-advisory-committee-for-safety-charter","summary":"The Federal Transit Administration (FTA) announces the reestablishment of the charter of the Transit Advisory Committee for Safety (TRACS). The previous TRACS charter expired on February 2, 2026. The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and FTA are committed to ensuring the safety of the Nation's public transportation systems and reducing safety risks to both riders and transit workers. Accordingly, the Secretary of Transportation (Secretary) has determined that reestablishing TRACS is necessary and in the public interest.","publishedAt":"2026-10-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20221","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities: Requests for Comments; Clearance of a Renewed Approval of Information Collection: Extended Operations (ETOPS) of Multi-Engine Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/02/2026-20221/agency-information-collection-activities-requests-for-comments-clearance-of-a-renewed-approval-of","summary":"In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FAA invites public comments about our intention to request the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) approval to renew an information collection. The collection involves practices that permitted certificated air carriers to operate two-engine airplanes over long range routes. The FAA uses this information collection to ensure that aircraft for long range flights are equipped to minimize diversions, to preclude and prevent diversions in remote areas, and to ensure that all personnel are trained to minimize any adverse impacts of a diversion.","publishedAt":"2026-10-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20210","title":"Application From the State of Georgia to the Surface Transportation Project Delivery Program and Proposed Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) Assigning Environmental Responsibilities to the State","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/02/2026-20210/application-from-the-state-of-georgia-to-the-surface-transportation-project-delivery-program-and","summary":"This notice announces that FHWA received and reviewed an application from the Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT) requesting participation in the Surface Transportation Project Delivery Program (Program). This Program allows for FHWA to assign, and States to assume, responsibilities under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (NEPA), and all or part of FHWA's responsibilities for environmental review, consultation, or other actions required under any Federal environmental law with respect to one or more Federal highway projects within the State. FHWA has determined the application to be complete and developed a draft MOU with GDOT outlining how the State would implement the Program with FHWA oversight. FHWA invites the public to comment on GDOT's request, including its application and the proposed MOU, which includes the proposed assignments and assumptions of environmental review, consultation, and other activities.","publishedAt":"2026-10-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20209","title":"Proposed Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) Assigning Certain Federal Environmental Responsibilities to the State of Georgia, Including National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) Authority for Certain Categorical Exclusions (CEs)","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/02/2026-20209/proposed-memorandum-of-understanding-mou-assigning-certain-federal-environmental-responsibilities-to","summary":"This notice announces that FHWA and the State of Georgia, acting by and through its State Department of Transportation, propose a MOU providing participation of the State in the CE Assignment Program. This program allows FHWA to assign its authority and responsibility for determining whether certain designated activities within the geographic boundaries of the State, as specified in the proposed MOU, are categorically excluded from preparation of an environmental assessment or an environmental impact statement under NEPA.","publishedAt":"2026-10-02","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-20207","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities: Requests for Comments; Clearance of a Renewed Approval of Information Collection: Drug and Alcohol Testing Program for Personnel Engaged in Specified Aviation Activities","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/02/2026-20207/agency-information-collection-activities-requests-for-comments-clearance-of-a-renewed-approval-of","summary":"In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FAA invites public comments about our intention to request the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) approval to renew an information collection. The Federal Register Notice with a 60-day comment period soliciting comments on the following collection of information was published on April 24, 2026. The information collected is used to determine program compliance or non-compliance of regulated aviation employers and contractors (including certificated foreign repair stations that must comply with the FAA's final rule, Drug and Alcohol Testing of Certificated Repair Station Employees Located Outside of the United States), conduct oversight planning, determine employers required to provide annual Management Information System (MIS) testing information, and communicate with entities subject to the program regulations.","publishedAt":"2026-10-02","source":"Federal Register"}]}
